reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure and every polynomial p with real coefficients, put S={w:E | norm(w)=1} with the subspace topology inherited from the norm topology of E, and let gamma=stdGaussian(E), the actual centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian on E. There exists a single proof family hfeature such that for every w in S, the actual scalar function f_w:E->R, f_w(x)=p.eval(inner_product(w,x)), is in MemLp exponent 2 under gamma. For that family, the map F:S->Lp R 2 gamma defined by F(w)=(hfeature(w)).toLp(f_w) is continuous for the standard L2 norm topology. In particular, membership asserts that each raw f_w is gamma-almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite L2 seminorm. Both this universal membership family and the continuity of the associated L2-valued map are conclusions; neither is a supplied hypothesis. The existential witnesses are proofs for the already specified functions under the same fixed Gaussian, not choices of alternative features or probability laws. F(w) is the genuine almost-everywhere equivalence class of f_w, and the conclusion concerns continuity of these classes in L2 norm. Equivalently, for each w0 in S and each epsilon>0 there exists delta>0 such that for all w in S, norm_E(w-w0)<delta implies norm_{L2(gamma)}(F(w)-F(w0))<epsilon. This formulation uses only weights remaining in S. Continuity of a selected pointwise representative family is not required. The theorem supplies no explicit numerical modulus. No nonzero-polynomial or positive-dimension premise is present. If p is zero, all the classes are zero. If E is zero dimensional, S is empty and the universal membership and continuity assertions are vacuous. The statement concerns the unit-parameter subspace and does not quantify nonunit weights.
objects: A finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with its Borel measurable structure; arbitrary real polynomial p; the exact unit-weight subtype S; fixed standard Gaussian gamma on E; raw polynomial ridge functions f_w(x)=p.eval(inner_product(w,x)); one family of genuine L2-membership proofs hfeature; and the lifted map F into the actual L2(gamma) quotient space.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. The parameter domain is S={w:E | norm(w)=1} with the subspace topology inherited from E. The function input x ranges over E and f_w has real values. gamma is the centered identity-covariance stdGaussian(E). p belongs to Polynomial R, the finite real-polynomial type. The codomain of F is Lp R 2 gamma with its standard L2 norm topology. No positive dimension is required. Completeness is not separately hypothesized and follows from finite dimensionality over R.
quantifiers: For every E with the stated structures and every p:Polynomial R, there exists hfeature:forall w:S, MemLp(f_w,2,gamma), such that the single map w->(hfeature(w)).toLp(f_w) is continuous on S. The universal unit-weight membership is inside one existential proof-family binder. The same E,p,gamma are fixed for every w. The continuity conclusion quantifies every point of S and all convergent parameter approaches within that subspace; equivalently it has the usual pointwise epsilon-delta quantifiers in the inherited metric and L2 norm.
assumptions: Only the displayed finite-dimensional real inner-product normed-space and Borel measurable-space structures, and a given arbitrary real polynomial p. There is no supplied hfeature, prior ridge integrability assumption, prior continuity assumption, nonzero polynomial, positive-dimensionality premise, or unit-vector existence premise. The equality norm(w)=1 is part of the quantified parameter subtype. Genuine L2 membership and L2-valued continuity are both produced by the theorem.
conclusion: There is a proof of genuine L2(stdGaussian(E)) membership for each actual function x->p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) at every exact unit vector w, and the resulting actual equivalence-class map from S to Lp R 2 (stdGaussian(E)) is continuous in L2 norm. In epsilon-delta terms, for every w0:S and epsilon>0 there exists delta>0 such that every w:S with norm_E(w-w0)<delta has norm_{L2(gamma)}(F(w)-F(w0))<epsilon.
scopes: The parameter topology is the inherited norm subspace topology on the exact unit set; the output topology is the L2 quotient norm topology under one fixed gamma. MemLp includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm. toLp forms the class of each displayed raw function; any selected representative need equal it only almost everywhere. Membership proofs do not choose a different function and do not alter the mathematical quotient class. Continuity is asserted for the class-valued map, without a pointwise-continuous representative-selection requirement. The statement gives no separate equality of Gaussian norms or explicit quantitative continuity bound. Zero polynomials are allowed and give the zero map; zero-dimensional E has empty S so the membership family and continuous empty-domain map are vacuous. The only parameter domain asserted is S.
constant_dependencies: There is no named estimate constant, prescribed radius beyond the exact unit condition, averaging denominator, or numerical continuity modulus. The map depends on E,p and the fixed standard Gaussian; a pointwise continuity delta may depend on the point w0, epsilon, and these fixed data. The theorem asserts existence of such a delta through continuity, without specifying its formula or a uniform/Lipschitz rate.
